attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 7.9). Installed AIDE (fixed the dead EPEL7 metalink, then installed from the subscribed rhel-7-server-rpms repo), verified the stock RHEL7 aide.conf already gives deep /etc coverage (CONTENT_EX rules for ~80 critical config paths plus a recursive /etc/ PERMS catch-all), initialized the database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, and proved detection works by modifying /etc/hosts (AIDE flagged the SHA256 change) then reverting it back to a clean state. Added /etc/cron.daily/aide-check to automatically run and log daily integrity reports to /var/log/aide/, then re-baselined to include that script itself so the database is fully current and clean. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and DB checksum baseline, issued a background shutdown -r now so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset, then verified the AIDE database checksum was unchanged, aide --check still reports clean, and the cron script/package survived the reboot.
